sector: HVAC components (brass and copper tubes and fittings for air-conditioner indoor and outdoor units, refrigeration lines)
headline: PAT grew from Rs 76.70 m to Rs 332.06 m over FY24-FY26 at a 28.39% ROCE, but FY26 revenue growth slowed to 9.0% and operating cash flow was Rs -430.08 m as inventory rose to 116 days, so the RHP's H1 FY27 cash flow and the price band decide the case.
red_flags: PAT Rs 76.70 m / 271.37 m / 332.06 m FY24-FY26; ROCE 28.39% and ROE 42.86% in FY26; cash tax 25.4% of cumulative PBT (pp. 86, 182)
Supplies eight of the top ten Indian HVAC makers; 96.91% of FY26 revenue from repeat customers; installed capacity up 50% in two years (pp. 174-175, 182)
Operating cash flow Rs +37.40 / -66.47 / -430.08 m against PAT; FY26 inventory days 116 vs 50 and borrowings Rs 1,532.11 m vs 658.75 m (pp. 87, 167)
Top-10 customers 89.71% of revenue (Amber 28.79%); Supplier 1 is 32.99% of expenses; no long-term supply contracts (pp. 24-26, 430)
Customs show-cause notice Rs 130.38 m (14.2% of net worth) at the Supreme Court; Rs 74.96 m FX loss on unhedged imports in FY26 (pp. 444, 461)
Rs 1,530.00 m of new units with no plant orders placed; peer P/Es run 19.08x to 141x, so the multiple method and the DCF are far apart (pp. 133-134, 179)
reference_note: Rs 115.82 = FY26 basic EPS of Rs 6.07 x 19.08, the lowest P/E in the DRHP's own peer table (Elin Electronics, p. 179). It is a reference to size the model, not a price band and not a view of the right price. The only priced transaction in the DRHP is the 29-Jan-2024 transfer among shareholders at Rs 34.66 per Rs 10 share, Rs 5.78 after the bonus and split (p. 190).

strengths: PAT Rs 76.70 m to Rs 332.06 m FY24-FY26; reported EBITDA margin 6.52% to 10.89% (p. 182)

Eligibility under Reg 6(1) reproduces: average operating profit Rs 366.37 m vs Rs 150 m (p. 475)
Related-party trade small: purchases Rs 28.57 m, sales Rs 2.65 m in FY26 (p. 90)
weaknesses: Operating cash flow Rs -430.08 m in FY26; cumulative CFO/PAT -67.5% (p. 87)
Top-10 suppliers 79.33%; Supplier 1 32.99%; 53.07% of raw material imported (pp. 21, 25)
Auditor changed 20-Sep-2025; audit trail not enabled at database level through FY26 (pp. 59, 95)
opportunities: Addressable HVAC-component market Rs 34.8 bn growing 24.46% a year to FY30, issuer-commissioned (p. 137)
Three new units (Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan) and new lines in heat exchangers, sheet metal and service valves; land already acquired (pp. 137-138)
Air-conditioner volume 12.8 m units in FY27 to 16.7 m in FY30 (9.3% CAGR) per CARE (p. 174)
Installed capacity 279.86 m units (FY24) to 419.26 m units (FY26) (p. 182)
threats: Customs show-cause notice of Rs 130.38 m, appeal pending at the Supreme Court (p. 461)
Unhedged import exposure: Rs 74.96 m FX loss in FY26 (p. 444)
Copper and brass price volatility; no long-term supply contracts described (pp. 25, 442)

Government localisation policy and import-duty changes affect demand (p. 137)
